summary: Bursting 429s for webhook callbacks after enabling CDN prefetch + lambda-edge retries
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightWave IoT reports sudden, sustained 429s for webhook callback endpoints after enabling an edge-level CDN prefetch rule + Lambda@Edge that retries on origin 5xx. The 429s started ~2026-03-12 06:00 UTC and affected their dedicated pool (us-east-1).

Impact:
- ~30% of webhook callbacks are rejected with 429 for ~45 minutes during morning traffic spike (reported customer-facing errors and downstream job failures).
- Affects background telemetry and critical device state updates for BrightWave fleet (thousands of small IoT devices).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer provisioned) in us-east-1
- Ingress via customer CDN (Edge) with Lambda@Edge that performs prefetch and rewrite for signed URLs
- Client traffic: many short-lived connections (IoT devices) + webhook fanout to 200k endpoints

Observed symptoms / Timeline:
- 2026-03-12 05:58 UTC: Customer enabled CDN prefetch rule to warm signed URLs.
- 2026-03-12 06:02 UTC: Burst of 429s begins for callback route /v1/webhooks/callback, correlating with CDN edges performing prefetches.
- 2026-03-12 06:20 UTC: Customer rolls back some CDN retry settings; 429 rate drops but remains above baseline.
- 2026-03-12 07:30 UTC: Support engagement opened.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Configure CDN to prefetch signed webhook callback URLs via HEAD/GET to our endpoint with a short TTL (10s).
2) Enable Lambda@Edge that rewrites auth headers and retries up to 2 times on 5xx.
3) Bulk trigger webhook fanout (simulated device update) over ~2 minutes.
4) Observe 429s returned from our API gateway and increased rate-limiter counters for that tenant.

Relevant logs / metrics (excerpt):
- rate-limiter: tenant_token_exhaustion spikes at 2026-03-12T06:02:12Z -> 06:10:00Z
- edge-proxy: incoming HEAD requests from multiple edge IPs, 10k/s aggregated for 90s
- auth-service: signed URL validation success, but repeated requests increase per-route counts
- sample access log lines:
  2026-03-12T06:02:13Z edge-34-... GET /v1/webhooks/callback 200 - cache-miss lambda-retry=1
  2026-03-12T06:02:13Z edge-54-... HEAD /v1/webhooks/callback 200 - cache-miss
  2026-03-12T06:02:14Z origin-01  POST /v1/webhooks/callback 429 tenant_quota_exhausted=1

Investigation notes:
- Rate accounting is currently counting HEAD and GET the same against the per-route token bucket. Prefetch HEADs from many edge nodes look identical to real client calls and are consuming burst credits.
- Lambda@Edge retries amplify the fanout: when an edge gets a 5xx from origin, lambda retries, so the origin sees duplicate requests from the same edge IP within a short window.
- CDN TTL of prefetch responses is very short (10s) so many edges revalidate concurrently, forming a microburst.
- Because BrightWave uses short-lived signed URLs and the CDN revalidates them frequently, cache-hit ratio is low leading to repeated origin requests.

Hypothesis:
1) Prefetch HEADs + short TTL + lambda retries caused a synchronized microburst across many edges that exhausted the customer's per-route burst quota and tripped tenant-level 429s.
2) Our current rate-limiter does not deduplicate/ignore HEAD prefetches and counts per-connection retried requests separately, which amplifies the apparent traffic.

Immediate mitigation / workaround applied:
- Support temporarily classified /v1/webhooks/callback as a high-burst route and enabled a short-lived emergency burst pool for BrightWave (dedicated) to keep critical callbacks through while we investigate.
- Recommended CDN config changes to customer: stop prefetching signed URLs OR increase TTL on prefetch responses; disable client-side lambda retries for origin 5xx during warmup.

Engineering actions planned:
- Rate-limiter change: implement configurable ignore-list for HEAD/OPTIONS for customers who use CDN prefetch (patch submitted, see related PR).
- Edge-proxy: add logic to tag requests with X-Edge-Prefetch when Lambda@Edge indicates prefetch so rate-limiter can apply different accounting. (Design doc linked.)
- Add telemetry: expose prefetch vs client metrics in console to help customers identify prefetch amplification.

Next steps / owner:
- Evan Chen (assignee): validate PR and run canary in staging by 2026-03-14.
- Customer (BrightWave): roll back CDN prefetch temporarily or increase TTL and confirm behavior.
- Support: monitor tenant quota usage for 48 hours after changes and coordinate incident follow-up.

Desired resolution criteria:
- No unexpected 429s for the callback route under similar prefetch settings, or documented config guidance that prevents recurrence.
workaround: Temporary dedicated burst pool added for BrightWave; advised to disable CDN prefetch or raise TTL and turn off lambda retries on origin 5xx.
resolution: (in progress) Engineering PR created to tag prefetch requests and to allow HEAD/OPTIONS exclusion from account counting. Once canary passes, will roll out to prod and update customer config guidance.
